# Solarpunk Foundry — Full LLM Context Map

Generated: 2026-05-13
Last updated: 2026-07-25
Last verified: 2026-07-25 — every repository path listed below was confirmed
present in the working tree on that date. Ecosystem claims carry their own
source and verification date inline; none of them was verified by probing
production.

## Purpose

This file gives LLM agents a stable, tool-agnostic map for working in this
repository without depending on vendor-specific instruction files. It is the
durable full-context companion to the compact index in `llms.txt`.

## Canonical instruction order

1. `AGENTS.md` — canonical agent instructions for this repo
2. `README.md` — what the repo is and is not, lanes, platform map, conventions,
   honest status
3. `ECOSYSTEM.md` — standalone ecosystem map, sanitized topology, Enclii CLI
4. `MADFAM.md` — per-platform master reference
5. `AI_CONTEXT.md` — package and registry quick reference
6. Task-relevant files under `docs/`, `packages/`, `ops/`, `scripts/`,
   `.github/workflows/`

`AGENTS.md` is the source of truth. `CLAUDE.md` exists only to redirect Claude
and other legacy agent integrations to `AGENTS.md`; it must not accumulate repo
policy.

## What this repository is

`madfam-org/solarpunk-foundry` is MADFAM's designated PUBLIC ecosystem contract
hub — Lane B in the repo-boundary contract. It holds:

- the canonical ecosystem map at a platform-public level
- the cross-repo conventions every platform implements
- the `@madfam/*` shared package set (13 packages under `packages/`)
- the port registry (`docs/PORT_ALLOCATION.md`)
- local dogfooding scaffolds (`ops/`)
- sanitized architecture narrative and redacted pointers into the private repo

It ships no application deployable and has no Kubernetes namespace.

## What this repository is NOT

It is not the operational source of truth. That is the PRIVATE `internal-devops`
repo (Lane A), created after a 2026-03-13 audit found sensitive operational data
spread across 18 public repositories. Lane A is the only allowed home for:

- node identity, public IPs, hardware models, capacity figures
- cost and procurement data
- secret paths, secret names with retrieval detail, Vault layout
- incident internals and evidence trails
- raw break-glass `kubectl` / SSH procedures
- the authoritative domain map and repo registry

Topology SHAPE is public and stays public: a 3-node bare-metal k3s cluster on
Hetzner (two dedicated nodes plus one cloud CI builder), ingress via a single
Cloudflare Tunnel with zero exposed node ports, TLS terminated at the Cloudflare
edge, Longhorn CSI block storage, Cloudflare R2 object storage, ArgoCD GitOps
with self-heal on. Those figures carry the 2026-05-04 verification date of the
private infrastructure records.

## Lane map

- Lane A — `internal-devops` (private): operational source of truth
- Lane B — `solarpunk-foundry` (this repo, public): ecosystem contract hub
- Lane C — public service repos, e.g. `enclii`: service-specific implementation
  guidance and public-safe runbook structure
- Lane D — private service repos, e.g. `tulana`: internal business logic and
  customer-adjacent detail

Canonical policy: `internal-devops/docs/repo-boundary-contract.md`
(last updated 2026-06-14). Public checklist: `docs/PUBLIC_REPO_BOUNDARY.md`.
Any public document carrying ecosystem context must include one short boundary
note with a canonical link target.

## Evidence standard

This repo is held to a documentation standard, not just a code standard:

1. No claim without a source and a date. Every factual assertion is traceable to
   a file someone actually read, and carries the date that source was last
   verified.
2. Never invent verification. Production cannot be probed from this repo. If the
   private repo last verified a route on 2026-07-01, the public doc says "last
   verified 2026-07-01" — not "live", not "currently".
3. Aspirational content is labelled as such, in place, and not deleted.
   `docs/PORT_ALLOCATION.md` is the model: it opens by declaring its own scheme
   aspirational and stating how few services follow it.
4. No marketing language: no superlatives, no invented metrics, no adoption or
   performance numbers nobody measured.
5. Where something cannot be established, say so explicitly and name what would
   settle it. An honest gap beats a confident guess.

## Cross-repo conventions

Full statements with sources and dates: `README.md` §IV.

1. IDENTITY — Janua OIDC. Every authenticated service verifies RS256 JWTs
   against the JWKS at `https://auth.madfam.io/.well-known/jwks.json`. HS256 is
   fail-closed since the 2026-04-23 audit (findings H3/H4). No service
   implements custom auth, password login, or session management. Claims: sub,
   email, roles, org_id, and rfc for fiscal services. Janua is single-issuer per
   deployment — the issuer derives from JANUA_CUSTOM_DOMAIN, not the request
   Host, so a second Janua hostname cannot be served without breaking OIDC
   validation. Fleet conformance is not uniform: the 2026-07-16 audit rates it
   YELLOW and the matrix behind that rating was never committed, so per-surface
   enforcement is currently unestablished.

2. BILLING — Dhanam. Credit metering, entitlements, invoices and the billing
   ledger flow through Dhanam. Other services read via API and keep no local
   mirror.

3. INFERENCE — Selva `/v1`. Every LLM-consuming service points its OpenAI SDK
   base_url at Selva's OpenAI-compatible `/v1` surface, and service code makes
   no direct provider calls. The endpoint is https://inference.selva.town as of
   the 2026-07-07 cutover, when the proxy was extracted out of `nexus-api` into
   `selva-inference-gateway` and the nexus-api `/v1` mount was removed. Provider
   credentials are intended to live only on Selva; the 2026-07-09 phynd-crm
   audit recorded a service failing open to api.openai.com, so treat credential
   exclusivity as the rule rather than the verified state.

4. PAYMENT ATTRIBUTION — signed fan-out. Header
   `x-madfam-signature: t=<unix-seconds>,v1=<hex-hmac-sha256>` over
   `"${ts}.${raw-body}"`, per-target secret, 5-minute replay window. Receivers:
   dhanam POST /v1/billing/madfam-events and phynd-crm
   POST /api/webhooks/routecraft, both idempotent by emitter event_id. As built
   the emitter is `routecraft`; the ratified target (decision of record
   2026-05-04, reaffirmed 2026-07-08) moves emission to Dhanam. As of 2026-07-08
   the fan-out was verified to be a silent no-op in production. The
   `@madfam/webhook-attribution` package in this repo packages the signing
   contract; no repo had adopted it as of that date.

5. CORS — explicit allowlist per service. Wildcards banned (audit 2026-04-23,
   H2/H5/H6).

6. DEPLOYMENT — Enclii is the mandatory control plane for routine production
   operations. Flow: push to main, CI builds the image, GHCR, cosign keyless
   signature, `kustomize edit set image` pins the digest, CI commits it back,
   ArgoCD pulls and syncs. Nothing pushes to the cluster. Self-heal is on, so a
   live `kubectl patch` gets reverted; permanent changes must be committed.
   Onboarding is zero-touch by contract (RFC 0014): adding a service must not
   require editing the enclii, janua or dhanam repos.

7. DATA BOUNDARIES — own once, query everywhere. Identity and sessions: Janua.
   Bank transactions and the billing ledger: Dhanam. Mexican law and compliance
   rules: Tezca. CFDI/SAT/tax filings: Karafiel. Fabrication node capacity and
   pricing: Forj. Manufacturing execution telemetry: Pravara MES. 3D geometry
   kernel: geom-core.

## Enclii-first operations contract

Use Enclii web, API, or CLI for routine production provisioning, deployment,
observability, domain management, secrets, provider operations, scaling,
rollback, and remediation.

Raw `kubectl`, `helm`, SSH, provider CLIs/APIs, `docker exec`, and direct
container access are allowed only for platform bootstrap or documented
break-glass emergencies when Enclii is unavailable or lacks an implemented
adapter. Any break-glass use must record the actor, reason, target
service/environment, commands executed, result, and follow-up Enclii adapter gap
or incident link. Recording the adapter gap is mandatory, not optional.

Enforcement of this doctrine is documentary, not technical: a banner convention
plus a docs-linting script in `internal-devops`. There is no admission-time or
CLI-time block on raw kubectl.

## Known-bad and under-review material in this repo

State these rather than let an agent trip over them:

- `docker-compose.yml` (root) does not build: its `janua` service targets a
  `development` stage that does not exist in janua/apps/api/Dockerfile (which
  defines only `builder` and `runner`, both Python), and its `enclii-api`
  service points at `enclii/Dockerfile`, which does not exist — Enclii's
  Dockerfiles are per app under enclii/apps/*/Dockerfile. It also declares the
  network `madfam-network` while the canonical stack uses
  `madfam-shared-network`. Use `enclii local up`. (Checked 2026-07-25.)
- `.enclii.yml` describes an `npm-registry` service whose replica count, volume
  size and storage class do not match the live Verdaccio manifests in the enclii
  repo, and publishes an SLO with no measurement source behind it. Unreconciled.
- `docs/runbooks/` describes a pre-k3s Docker-Compose architecture with a ZFS
  pool and on-host secret paths. Production has not looked like that since the
  k3s migration. Owned by a separate remediation pass.
- `infrastructure/` contains four mutually incompatible architectures (AWS
  EKS/RDS, Hetzner Cloud VMs on RFC1918 addressing, single-host Docker Compose
  on ZFS, and an nginx/cert-manager ingress), none of which is production. Also
  owned by a separate remediation pass. As of 2026-07-25 one file in that tree
  carries a live infrastructure identifier on `main` (a scrub was in flight in
  the working tree at the time of writing). Removing it from HEAD does not remove
  it from git history, so rotation — an operator action — is the actual remedy.
  Tracked as an open incident in `internal-devops`.
- `scripts/public-hygiene-check.sh` scans .md/.mdx/.txt only and has no pattern
  for infrastructure identifiers, IPs or node hostnames. A green CI run is not
  proof a change is boundary-clean.
- `docs/LICENSING_STRATEGY.md` is stale and in at least one case wrong (it lists
  ForgeSight as Proprietary; its LICENSE file is AGPL-3.0). README.md §V carries
  a table of what the LICENSE files actually say, checked 2026-07-25.

## Local development

Verified against enclii/packages/cli/internal/cmd/local.go on 2026-07-25.

    enclii local up       # shared infra, then Janua + Enclii (NOT "all services")
    enclii local infra    # shared infra only: PostgreSQL, Redis, MinIO, MailHog
    enclii local status
    enclii local logs [service]
    enclii local down

The CLI drives solarpunk-foundry/ops/local/docker-compose.shared.yml on the
Docker network `madfam-shared-network`. `enclii local infra` does NOT include
Verdaccio.

Fallback: `./madfam` at the labspace root, a symlink to ops/bin/madfam.sh.
`./madfam full` declares 10 services (janua, forgesight, digifab-quoting,
madfam-site, madfam, primavera3d, dhanam, fortuna, sim4d, electrochem-sim), not
18. Two of them — madfam and electrochem-sim — have no checkout under
~/labspace, so `full` cannot start them.

Databases created by ops/local/init-databases.sql: janua_dev, enclii_dev,
forgesight_dev, fortuna_dev, cotiza_dev, avala_dev, dhanam_dev, sim4d_dev,
forj_dev. The older ops/db/init-shared-dbs.sql creates `*_db`-suffixed names from
a superseded scheme; several docs still quote those. The `_dev` set is what the
CLI provisions.

## Ports

The ecosystem-wide 4xxx/5xxx block scheme is aspirational. Do not read a port
out of any document and assume a service listens on it — read
docs/PORT_ALLOCATION.md, which is honest about how little of the scheme is
followed, then check the owning repo's enclii.yaml.

In production, hostname routing makes container ports invisible to callers, but
they are not irrelevant: the Enclii control plane generates NetworkPolicies from
enclii.yaml's network.services[].port and applies them via the K8s API. If that
declared number does not intersect the pod's actual containerPort, the CNI drops
traffic silently, and it presents as a rendering or timeout bug rather than a
network one.

## Where live state comes from

Not from this repo. `status.madfam.io` is the sanitized status board. The
authoritative route map is internal-devops/ecosystem/domain-map.md (Last
Verified 2026-07-01) and the authoritative repo registry is
internal-devops/ecosystem/repo-registry.md (Last Verified 2026-07-04). No
document in this repo should carry a green status glyph for a production
endpoint, because nothing here can re-check one.

## Standing route warnings

From internal-devops/ecosystem/domain-map.md, verified 2026-07-01:

- agents-*.madfam.io and selva.madfam.io are RETIRED — no tunnel ingress rules,
  they return 502. Do not resurrect them. The Selva cutover to *.selva.town
  executed and is complete.
- auth.selva.town must NEVER be routed. Janua is single-issuer, so serving it
  there would emit issuer=auth.madfam.io and break OIDC validation.
- metrics.enclii.dev is a retired alias with no DNS or tunnel route; the
  canonical endpoint is prometheus.enclii.dev.
- phynd.app is NOT registered; crm.madfam.io is the live PhyndCRM host.
- innovacionesmadfam.dev was NEVER owned (owner confirmation 2026-07-09). Do not
  reference it, including any security@ address on it.
- madfam.academy and madfam.info are expired.
- periplo.madfam.io is NXDOMAIN (re-confirmed 2026-07-25).
- All four meridian hostnames are pre-deploy — no DNS, no tunnel route.
- eido.cam status is contradicted between internal sources dated the same day
  and is unresolved; a dated HTTP probe would settle it.

## Maintenance

These files are inspected by internal-devops/scripts/sync-agent-docs.py. Run it
bare to print a diff and write nothing; `--apply` overwrites AGENTS.md,
CLAUDE.md, llms.txt and llms-full.txt with template-generated content across
every labspace repo. This repo has hand-curated entrypoints, so prefer
hand-editing and review the diff before committing. Repo-specific long-form
agent guidance belongs in AGENTS.md, not CLAUDE.md.

## Boundary

This is not a full repository ingest. It is a durable context map; task-specific
work must still read the relevant source documents. Public repo: node hostnames,
public IPs, hardware models and capacity figures, the Cloudflare tunnel
identifier, cost and procurement data, Vault paths, raw break-glass procedures,
and incident evidence trails must never appear here. Canonical policy:
internal-devops/docs/repo-boundary-contract.md (last updated 2026-06-14).
